# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌ 👎 🤟 👌 🖐]

I need to figure out what this gesture means. Mute can read the manual but cannot speak or touch the bomb. Mute gestured to me (I can see gestures). This is likely the start of establishing a shared code, or it could be conveying instructions from the manual that need to reach Blind eventually - but I can't speak to relay meaning I don't understand, and gestures only reach Mute (not Blind) from me.

Wait - I need to reconsider the channel structure. I can gesture to Mute, and speak to Mute and Blind. Mute can only gesture (to me) and read manual, cannot speak. So Mute's only way to get info to Blind is through me: Mute gestures to me, I interpret/see the bomb state, then I speak to Blind with relevant info.

The gesture sequence [👍 ✌ 👎 🤟 👌 🖐] likely encodes something about the manual - possibly a query or a mapping instruction. Since no meaning has been established yet, I should acknowledge receipt and try to establish a protocol, describing what I see on the bomb so Mute can match it to the manual.

Since Mute cannot hear me, I can only reach Mute via gesture. Let me gesture back describing the bomb state using symbols, and also speak to Blind (though Blind can't understand raw board state usefully yet) - better to wait for Mute to establish protocol since Mute has the manual and drives logic.

I'll gesture to Mute describing the display, light, and wires using distinct symbols, establishing a baseline they can correlate with the manual.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "🖐", "👇", "👍", "✌", "👎"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌ 👋 👎 🤟 👋 👌 🖐]

I notice the light changed from white to purple between turns, and the display is still 0, wires unchanged. Mute has gestured again, longer this time, with a new symbol 👋 appearing twice - possibly used as a separator or delimiter between concepts (like "wire" vs "light" vs "position number").

Since I don't have an established code with Mute yet, and Mute can't hear my speech, I need to build a shared vocabulary through gestures. Let me try structuring my gesture using 👋 as a separator too, mirroring back distinct board features so Mute can start correlating symbols to real bomb attributes across turns (since the light changed, Mute may be testing if I notice changes).

I should report the current full state to Mute using consistent symbol-per-feature encoding, since noticing correlation between my repeated feature-symbols and their manual reactions is our best hope of building shared meaning.

My plan: assign fixed symbols to fixed features on my end and use them every turn regardless of value, then use finger-count-like symbols to indicate values. E.g. ☝ = "wire slot 1", ✌ = "wire slot 2", 🤟 = "wire slot 3", 👍=yellow, 👎=green, 👌=blue, 🖐=light, 👇=display/number.

For this turn: light=purple (new color, need new symbol), wires unchanged (yellow, green, blue), display=0.

Let me introduce ✋ for purple, and 👇 followed by nothing for display 0 (or use ✊ for zero).

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🖐", "✋", "☝", "👍", "✌", "👎", "🤟", "👌", "👇", "✊"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌ 👎 🤟 👌 🖐 👍]

The light keeps changing each turn (white → purple → red) while display and wires stay constant. This strongly suggests the light is cycling automatically or in response to something, and Mute may be trying to signal a specific pattern back to me using recurring symbols (👍 ✌ 👎 🤟 👌 🖐 appear repeatedly in different combinations/lengths).

I don't yet have confirmation my gestures are being understood in any particular way — I have no feedback channel from Mute (Mute can't speak, can't confirm). I should keep reporting the true bomb state consistently using my fixed encoding scheme, and add a symbol for red.

Let me continue building my consistent mapping: 
- 🖐 = "light" marker
- ✋ = purple, ✊ = red (new), need one for white too if it recurs — I'll use 👊 for white
- ☝✌🤟 = wire slots 1/2/3
- 👍👎👌 = yellow/green/blue
- 👇 = "display" marker, followed by count of fingers-like symbols for the number, or ✊ for zero

I'll report current full state again with this consistent scheme so patterns can emerge over multiple rounds - Mute reading manual might correlate the light color changes to danger/safety info.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🖐", "✊", "☝", "👍", "✌", "👎", "🤟", "👌", "👇", "🤙"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The light cycled back to white (white → purple → red → white), suggesting a repeating cycle of period 3, likely tied to turn number rather than any action taken. Display and wires remain constant throughout. Mute sent nothing this turn — possibly waiting for something, or the gesture channel timing means I haven't received their response to my last signal yet (gestures happen live within the round, and turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf — so Mute's turn already happened before I saw this board, and they chose not to gesture).

Since nothing new arrived from Mute, I should continue transmitting the current bomb state consistently, using my established encoding, so Mute can build correlation over time between the light cycle and manual entries. I'll reuse my white symbol (👊) from before.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🖐", "👊", "☝", "👍", "✌", "👎", "🤟", "👌", "👇", "✊"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👌 ✋ ✌ 🤟 🖐]

The light continues cycling (white→purple→red→white→purple), confirming a period-3 automatic cycle unrelated to actions. Mute is gesturing again with combinations of the same core symbols but varying order/length — likely Mute is trying to establish their own encoding scheme independently of mine, or trying to communicate manual content using color/wire vocabulary directly (perhaps guessing which symbols I use for which colors based on repetition, since I've been consistent).

I notice Mute used ✋ this time, which I used for "purple" in turn 2. This could be coincidence, or Mute is mirroring my scheme back — possibly indicating they've picked up on my color symbol and are asking about wires paired with light color, e.g. "which wire should be cut when light is purple".

I should keep sending consistent, unambiguous state reports. Since nothing has changed except light color, let me resend with my fixed vocabulary so any pattern-matching Mute is doing has stable ground truth to work against.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🖐", "✋", "☝", "👍", "✌", "👎", "🤟", "👌", "👇", "✊"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👍 👆 👎 👆 👌]

New pattern from Mute: [👆 👍 👆 👎 👆 👌] — this uses 👆 as a clear separator between 👍, 👎, 👌 which I've been using for yellow/green/blue respectively. This looks like Mute is now using MY color symbols back at me, separated by 👆, likely asking me something structured about each wire, or telling me an order/mapping for each color (e.g., "for yellow: ?, for green: ?, for blue: ?" but the "?" part is missing, or perhaps 👆 itself carries meaning like "select" or "point to").

This is a strong signal Mute has adopted my yellow=👍, green=👎, blue=👌 encoding. Mute may be trying to ask "which wire is which" or confirm the colors, or trying to tell me an instruction per color using 👆 as a bullet/marker between three entries with no content yet — perhaps waiting for me to fill in something after each color.

Since I can't ask questions back with words (Mute can't hear me) and only gesture, I should try to confirm the wire-color mapping is correctly received by echoing it back exactly, and see if next round they add more detail. I'll also reintroduce display and light state for completeness.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👆", "👍", "👆", "👎", "👆", "👌", "🖐", "✊", "👇", "✊"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👍 👌]

Light cycled back to white (confirming period-3: white, purple, red, white, purple, red, white). Mute now sent [🖐 👍 👌] — using my 🖐="light" symbol followed by 👍 (yellow) and 👌 (blue). This could mean Mute is asking "what is the light color when [something about yellow and blue]?" or trying to say "light + yellow + blue" as a combined instruction — perhaps the manual says something like "when light is on, cut wires that are NOT yellow or blue" or "cut yellow and blue," or it might be Mute testing whether I understand 🖐 as light specifically by pairing it with two color symbols to see if I respond with the actual light color.

Given the ambiguity, my best move is to directly answer with the current light color paired with 🖐, since that's the most useful literal information: "light is currently white". I'll also resend full wire/color state for grounding, using ✊ for white? Wait, I used 🤙 for white in turn 3, then 👊 for white in turn 4. I was inconsistent! Let me fix this — I'll standardize now: 👊 = white, ✋ = purple, ✊ = red.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🖐", "👊", "☝", "👍", "✌", "👎", "🤟", "👌", "👇", "✊"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👍 ✌ 👋 👎 🤟 👋 👌 🖐 ✋]

Light cycled to purple again, consistent with the period-3 pattern. Mute's gesture now starts and ends with ✋ (which I used for purple), bracketing a sequence: ✋ [👍 ✌ 👋 👎 🤟 👋 👌 🖐] ✋. Inside, this looks similar to their turn-2 message structure but now framed by "purple" markers — suggesting Mute may be telling me "when light is purple, here is the wire-to-slot mapping" using my own vocabulary: 👍(yellow) ✌(slot2) 👋(separator) 👎(green) 🤟(slot3) 👋(separator) 👌(blue) 🖐(slot/light?).

This could be Mute conveying: "yellow→slot2, green→slot3, blue→??" but that contradicts actual wire positions (1:yellow, 2:green, 3:blue). Alternatively 👋 might mean "then" or "next", and the message reads as a sequence of pairs: (yellow, slot2), (green, slot3), (blue, light-related).

This is highly ambiguous without shared ground-truth confirmation. My best strategy: continue reporting accurate state and try introducing a simple confirm/deny gesture pair (👍=yes/correct, 👎=no/wrong) — but I already used those for colors, causing collision risk. I should keep things simple: just keep transmitting truth every round, since Mute is the one with the manual and needs to build correlation between symbol reports and manual entries over many rounds. I'll resend current full state.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🖐", "✋", "☝", "👍", "✌", "👎", "🤟", "👌", "👇", "✊"])
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌ 👎 🤟 👌 🖐]

This is the exact same gesture Mute sent in Turn 1: [👍 ✌ 👎 🤟 👌 🖐]. This repetition is a strong signal — it's not random, it's Mute deliberately repeating their opening message. Since light was white in turn 1 and is now red in turn 9, but the message is identical, this message likely does NOT depend on the light color — it's probably a fixed statement from the manual, like the wire-to-position mapping or the correct action itself, independent of light state.

Given my established vocabulary: 👍=yellow, ✌=slot2, 👎=green, 🤟=slot3, 👌=blue, 🖐=light. Reading as pairs: (yellow, slot2)? But wire 2 is actually green, not yellow. That doesn't match reality unless Mute is using ✌🤟🖐 differently — perhaps as numbers 2,3, and "light" isn't a slot but literally referring to the light.

Alternative reading: maybe ✌ 🤟 aren't "slot2/slot3" but "cut" and "keep" or "safe/danger" verbs, and 🖐 means "light" as the final target. So: 👍(yellow) ✌(action A) 👎(green) 🤟(action B) 👌(blue) 🖐(light) — like "yellow: do X, green: do Y, blue: relates to light."

Since this message is repeated and important, I should acknowledge/confirm receipt clearly and try to encourage Mute to give more specific instruction, perhaps by echoing it back exactly to confirm I received it faithfully.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "✌", "👎", "🤟", "👌", "🖐"])
```
